claims.quote: A de novo mutation (c.C316G > A, p.A106T) in the human GABA type-A receptor γ2 subunit gene (GABRG2) has been recurrently identified in patients with DEE.
In this study, we generated a knock-in mouse model replicating the human GABRG2(A106T) variation (Gabrg2+/A105T in mouse).

claims.object_text: Gabrg2+/A105T mouse displays seizures and early mortality
claims.quote: Gabrg2+/A105T mice displayed early mortality, spontaneous seizures, and heightened seizure susceptibility.
including impaired spatial learning and memory
as well as increased anxiety-like behavior

claims.object_text: reduced γ2 subunit protein expression in hippocampus
claims.quote: Reduced γ2 subunit protein expression was detected in the hippocampus of mutant mice, but not other brain regions.

claims.object_text: impaired synaptic GABAergic inhibition (decreased mIPSC amplitude)
claims.quote: Electrophysiological recordings revealed a significant decrease in the amplitude of miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents (mIPSCs), indicating impaired synaptic GABAergic inhibition.
hippocampal transcriptome profiling provided evidence of neuroinflammation

claims.object_text: neuronal loss and microglia activation prior to seizure onset
claims.quote: histological analysis demonstrated neuronal loss and microglia activation prior to seizure onset.

claims.object_text: neuroinflammatory processes may exacerbate epileptogenesis in Gabrg2+/A105T mice
claims.quote: These findings indicate that neuroinflammatory processes, a major theme in acquired epilepsies, may potentially exacerbate epileptogenesis in Gabrg2+/A105T mice.
The knock-in mouse model serves as a potential model for evaluating anti-inflammatory therapies as adjunct treatments for drug-resistant DEEs.
